radiology_report:
Radboudumc
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 November 2024
Examination: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 8.8 ng/mL with PI-RADS 5 lesion on prior imaging; assess for interval progression.
FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 47.0 mL in volume with preserved zonal anatomy. T2-weighted imaging reveals a focal hypointense lesion measuring approximately 12 mm in the left peripheral zone at the apical/base junction. This area demonstrates marked restricted diffusion on DWI sequences and corresponding early intense enhancement on DCE, consistent with a PI-RADS v2.1 score of 5. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle involvement is seen.
IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone (apical/base).
Prostate volume 47.0 mL; PSA density 0.19 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical stage cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7517428.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: The patient attended a routine primary care follow-up with a PSA measurement of 4.5 ng/mL, representing a notable increase from the July 2023 baseline of 2.3 ng/mL. Given the accelerating trend and mild lower urinary tract symptoms, a repeat transperineal biopsy was coordinated through the regional urology pathway, and cardiovascular risk factors were optimised with current lipid-lowering and antihypertensive regimens. The patient was advised to attend the scheduled outpatient re-evaluation for prior prostate cancer diagnosis to review the forthcoming histological results and discuss long-term management options.

pathology_report:
Specimen: Transperineal prostate biopsy, 12 October 2024. Microscopic evaluation demonstrates adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. Perineural invasion is present, and no cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. The tumour is situated in the peripheral zone, apical/base left. Histological assessment remains consistent with ISUP grade group 2 disease across the available biopsy timepoint.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 4.
